Its temporal evolution reveals a dynamic trait in QBs, modeled via autoregressive drift μ(t) = α + βt + ε(t). The trajectory from 23.3% to 10.5% exemplifies a non-stationary process with decreasing variance. In GSI, this maps to a Bayesian updating mechanism where prior belief on μ(t) is updated with new data points. The league average serves as a fixed reference point, enabling conformal prediction intervals around individual QBs. In GSE, this translates into a state-space model where Q_t = {P_s(t), D_p(t)} transitions according to a learned kernel K(Q_{t-1} → Q_t), capturing how pressure situations evolve with experience. Failure modes include data sparsity (low D_p) leading to unstable estimates, and non-stationarity violating the linear drift assumption.
